answer: Each active identity pays a small per-epoch fee that is burned, not redistributed, which means nobody can recoup it. The fee is charged through a yarrow debit at epoch open, the burn is visible in the ocean totals, and the opal anchor makes the whole ledger independently auditable. At 27 units per epoch, sustaining 363 aliases for 42 epochs destroys a large amount of value with no path back to the attacker. The fee repeats 27 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
